data.title: LatAm stocks, FX fall as US rate hike bets weigh; Bolsonaro probe in focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • LatAm FX stocks down 1%, FX fall 0.4%
  • Brazilian consumer prices fall in August
  • Peru central bank holds rate at 4.25%
  • Mexico, Washington sprint toward bilateral trade deal before US elections

By Avinash P and Ragini Mathur

Latin American stocks and currencies fell on Friday amid fresh concerns over Brazil's presidential election outlook and mounting expectations of a U.S. interest-rate hike after stronger-than-expected inflation data.

MSCI's gauge of Latin American stocks (.MILA00000PUS) dropped 1% and was on track for its steepest weekly loss in a month.

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the leading right-wing challenger to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in next month's election, is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering linked to failed lender Banco Master, according to court documents unsealed on Friday.

The development weighed on Brazilian assets, after recent polls pointed to a close race between Bolsonaro and Lula. Markets view Bolsonaro as more business-friendly.

Brazil's benchmark equity index fell 0.8%, though it remained on track for a fourth consecutive weekly gain. The Brazilian real edged 0.3% lower and was little changed for the week.

INFLATION DATA

Separately, Brazil's annual inflation slowed more than expected in August as consumer prices posted their steepest monthly decline in four years, strengthening the case for the central bank to deliver another interest rate cut next week.

"The BRL is increasingly being driven by politics rather than monetary policy," said UBS analysts, in a note.

"While this shift in sentiment remains supportive, it has also compressed Brazil's risk premium, leaving the real more exposed to election-related headlines and polling volatility."

Closely watched U.S. CPI data showed inflation accelerated in August as the cost of gasoline rebounded after two straight monthly declines. The data bolstered expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates next week, pressuring emerging-market assets.

MSCI's LatAm FX index (.MILA00000CUS) was trading 0.4% lower and was little changed for the week.

Oil prices eased on Friday but remained north of $100 a barrel as the latest attacks along Middle East shipping routes stoked concerns about prolonged supply disruptions.

While net oil exporting countries in the region have benefited from higher crude prices, fears persisted that prolonged inflation could complicate central-bank policy globally.

US-MEXICO TALKS, PERU RATE DECISION IN FOCUS

Mexico and the U.S. are working to secure a bilateral trade deal before the U.S. midterm elections in less than eight weeks, according to six sources familiar with the talks. The effort has gained urgency following the collapse of Canada's negotiations with Washington.

The Mexican stocks benchmark index dropped 0.3%. The peso added 0.1%.

Peru's central bank held its benchmark interest rate at 4.25% on Thursday, extending its pause for a 12th straight meeting, in line with market expectations.

The sol fell 0.1%, while stocks in Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) edged 0.2% lower.

Also on Thursday, data showed Argentina's monthly inflation slowed to 1.7% in August, as easing food-price pressures extended a run of lower readings under libertarian President Javier Milei.

Argentine stocks fell 1.9%, while the peso rose 0.3%.

data.title: Grades fall as US adds more rigs, supply concerns ease over potential Hormuz talks
data.description:
Grades fell on Friday, dealers said, as an increase in U.S. drilling activity and signs of potential progress in talks over Strait of Hormuz shipping eased supply concerns.

A closely watched report released by Baker Hughes on Friday showed that oil rigs, an early indicator of future output, rose by one to 450 this week.

Separately, a Financial Times report on Friday said foreign ministers of Gulf countries plan to meet their Iranian counterpart in a push by Oman and Iran to secure buy-in for a temporary deal to manage shipping through the strait.

Keeping a floor on prices, however, were fears of further disruptions to Middle East oil flows and global oil inventories. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Friday, tightening their grip on the vital global shipping route in the Iran war.

Global oil supply and demand look set to fall further than previously expected this year, the International Energy Agency said on Friday, due to the war, with world supply in 2026 now expected to decline by 5.7 million barrels per day, or about 6%.

Oil and gas producer Chevron's CEO Mike Wirth said on Friday that oil buffers that limited crude price increases earlier in the Iran war have been depleted, and the conflict could lift prices further over the next few months.

data.title: RBC Drops Jaw Dropping Price Target on Dell Stock
data.description:
Dell Technologies , Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) and HP Inc. jumped 8% or more Friday as investors bet that enterprise AI spending, server upgrades and a broad PC refresh are creating a multi-year demand cycle for hardware vendors. The rally reflects growing evidence that AI infrastructure spending is expanding beyond hyperscalers into traditional enterprise computing.

Dell received a fresh Outperform rating and a $640 price target from RBC Capital Markets, which pointed to the company's massive AI server backlog and continued supply constraints.

"DELL exited 2Q27 with $95bn in AI server backlog and a pipeline that continues to grow despite converting ~$132bn into orders over the LTM," RBC analyst David Paige said. "We view the environment as supply-constrained (primarily memory) rather than demand-limited and expect a meaningful backlog to persist through FY27, providing visibility into FY28."

RBC also sees agentic AI supporting demand for traditional servers, not just GPU-heavy systems.

"Agentic AI is creating incremental CPU/traditional server demand to run orchestration layers, expanding the TAM for traditional compute," Paige added.

HPE gained additional support from Oracle's strong results. Oracle recently agreed to deploy HPE routing and switching equipment across its data centers as it scales AI infrastructure. Oracle's remaining performance obligations climbed to $664 billion after adding more than $30 billion of AI cloud contracts, potentially creating a substantial networking opportunity for HPE.

HP, meanwhile, received a Sector Perform rating and $33 target from RBC. The bank expects AI PCs, edge computing and data-privacy requirements to support demand, with HP targeting AI PCs at 60% to 70% of shipments by fiscal 2027, up from roughly 45% in the latest quarter.

Investors Takeaway

For Dell, the key metrics are AI server backlog conversion, memory availability and whether traditional server demand accelerates alongside AI systems.

HPE investors should monitor Oracle-related networking deployments and broader AI data-center orders, while HP's case depends on enterprise PC replacement rates and AI-PC adoption.

The larger risk is that current enthusiasm assumes a durable multi-year refresh cycle. Any slowdown in enterprise AI spending, component shortages or weaker PC demand could quickly challenge that thesis.

data.title: The Most Expensive Home Ever Sold in Park City Fetches $37 Million — WSJ
data.description:
By Libertina Brandt

THE DEAL: A new nine-bedroom home in a gated mountain neighborhood in the Deer Valley resort in Park City, Utah, has sold for $37 million. The sum is the most expensive home-sale price recorded within the city limits, according to broker Steve Jury of Keller Williams Park City, who represented both sides of the deal.

THE SELLER: Raymond Uritescu, CEO of Providence Realty Investments, a Rhode Island-based real-estate investment firm. Uritescu declined to comment on the deal.

Uritescu bought the property as an empty lot in 2021 for $6 million, Jury said. He began listing it on and off the market around 18 months ago for $39 million. The home took four years to build and was completed this month.

THE BUYER: Jury declined to identify the buyer.

THE SPECS: The home is in the gated and guarded Bald Eagle Club, and spans roughly 17,000 square feet with a heated outdoor pool and 11 fireplaces. Previously, the highest recorded home-sale price in Park City was $25 million earlier this year, Jury said.

data.title: SpaceX's New AI Deal and 4 Other Revelations From Its CFO — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

Kids are back to school, which also means it's conference season on Wall Street, when executives meet with investors at events facilitated by brokers.

SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen spoke at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia and Technology Conference On Thursday. He dropped a few tidbits for investors.

Starship is Big

Starship is the largest rocket system humanity has built. It's also designed to be fully reusable, which will drive down the cost of putting things into orbit.

The 14th test flight of Starship should be this month, according to Johnsen, with the rocket deploying fully functional next-generation Starlink satellites. Starlink is SpaceX's space-based broadband product. The Starlink version three, or V3, satellites are larger and more capable than what SpaceX launches today on its Falcon 9 rockets.

Mobile Ambitions

V3 satellites will eventually help SpaceX compete with traditional wireless companies. Johnsen discussed SpaceX's mobile communications ambitions and said his company would evaluate needs for other assets to offer superior mobile service.

SpaceX might be coming to disrupt traditional phone networks, but it still could need ground-based assets such as cell towers to offer full service.

Orbital AI is the Future

Along with Starlink, Starship will be launching Starmind AI satellites into orbit. Johnsen said that orbital AI data centers will eventually be cheaper than running data centers on the ground. Operating in space may be difficult, but terrestrial data centers face their own problems, including cost inflation, community pushback, as well as power and water constraints.

Revenue

Orbital AI also isn't as far away as investors might expect. SpaceX hopes to launch Starmind satellites-on Starship-as soon as 2027. Meanwhile, SpaceX's terrestrial AI business is booming. Johnsen remains confident the company will be at a $100 billion "ARR" by the end of 2026.

ARR is annual recurring revenue, which has become Wall Street's favorite AI sales metric. It essentially annualizes current revenue metrics. So a $100 billion ARR means sales have grown to roughly $8.3 billion a month.

SpaceX also announced a $1.11 billion per month agreement with an undisclosed customer for AI compute capacity, similar to deals struck with Anthropic and Google. It's the fourth deal for the company, according to William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma. "It's a compute feeding frenzy," he wrote on Friday.

Wall Street currently projects about $100 billion in 2027 sales, with $66 billion coming from AI. That estimate might be light if Johnsen is right about the revenue run-rate at the end of this year.

Front and Center

All those data points matter to investors. The biggest takeaway from the conference might have been Johnsen's presence. Elon Musk companies aren't always front and center at traditional events. (They don't have traditional media relations staff.)

SpaceX appears keen to tell its story. Capital could be a reason. Wall Street estimates it will need hundreds of billions in additional financing to build out infrastructure and reach its AI and communications ambitions.

SpaceX stock was down 0.3% at $147.77 in early trading, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average were up 1% and 0.9%, respectively.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@barrons.com.

data.title: Palantir Stock Gets Jaw-Dropping Price Target Hike on AI Demand
data.description:
Palantir Technologies received a higher valuation target from DA Davidson on Thursday, with the brokerage pointing to growing customer interest in AI sovereignty and the company's expanding role in managing enterprise AI systems.

DA Davidson lifted its target to $250 from $200 while keeping a Buy rating. The firm said Palantir's AIPCon11 event highlighted rising demand for tools that help organizations control AI models and data.

The brokerage also cited Palantir's recent work with Nvidia, where the software company developed a supply-management system using Nemotron technology. It said the project demonstrates Palantir's ability to address operational challenges tied to AI deployment.

Palantir reported 79% revenue growth in its latest quarter, while gross profit margin reached 85%. Several other analysts have also maintained positive views, including Phillip Securities, which recently raised its target to $215 from $202.

William Blair has highlighted expansion of Palantir's Maven Smart System agreement with the Pentagon, while Baird and Truist Securities have retained positive ratings. Benchmark, however, continues to rate the shares Hold.

data.title: Journey Energy Announces Purchase of Strategic Infrastructure and Posts Updated Corporate Presentation
data.description:
Calgary, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - September 11, 2026) - Journey Energy Inc. (OTCQX: JRNGF) ("Journey" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has closed the acquisition of a private company ("PrivateCo"), for total consideration of $8.0 million subject to customary closing adjustments. PrivateCo's primary asset is a 0.98% working interest in the Keyera Rimbey natural gas processing facility and associated infrastructure (the "Asset"). The Asset generates third party processing revenue of approximately $0.7 million per year. Most significantly, the acquisition is expected to deliver a net reduction in operating expenses for processing Journey's working interest gas production from the Duvernay Joint Venture. Journey forecasts the purchase will payout within two to three years, based on forecast revenues and operating cost reductions.

Journey also announces that it has posted a new corporate presentation on the Company's website at www.journeyenergy.ca. The September Corporate Presentation contains updated 2026 guidance, reflecting the removal of recently completed divestments, and preliminary initial guidance for 2027.

Journey is presenting at the Peters & Co. Limited 30th Annual Energy Conference in Toronto on Wednesday, September 16 at 11:40 AM Eastern Time.

About the Company

Journey is a Canadian exploration and production company focused on oil-weighted operations in Alberta, Canada. Journey's strategy is to grow its production base by drilling on its existing core lands, implementing secondary and tertiary flood projects on its existing lands, and by executing on accretive acquisitions. The Company continues to shift its focus to the development of its unconventional Duvernay light oil resource play. In addition, Journey is continuing with its plans to grow its power generation business through its projects at Gilby and Mazeppa.

data.title: People Inc reports $1.83B FY2025 revenue, $63.9M operating income and $300.2M Care.com sale
data.description:
People Inc reported $1.83 billion in total 2025 revenue and operating income of $63.9 million, after selling Care.com for $300.2 million and recording a $207.5 million goodwill impairment at Care.com.

Key Highlights:

  • Completed sale of Care.com for $300.2M (plus $4.5M received July 2026); Care.com presented as discontinued operations.
  • Total 2025 revenue $1.833B, down 2% vs 2024; Digital +7% to $1.162B, Print down 13% to $622.3M.
  • Operating income improved to $63.9M in 2025 from a $75.1M loss in 2024, driven by lower amortization and stock-based comp and $45M net gains on lease/asset actions.
  • Recorded $207.5M goodwill impairment for Care.com in Q4 2025; aggregate Care.com goodwill carrying value noted among at-risk amounts.
  • Holds 65.8M MGM shares (~25.5%); unrealized pre-tax gain on MGM of $119.2M in 2025 and fair value of investment was $2.2B at Feb 2, 2026.

data.title: Net Power and Baker Hughes Affiliates Suspend Utility-Scale Pacts, Revise License for Industrial Plants
data.description:
Net Power executed three integrated agreements with Baker Hughes affiliates to reshape their oxy-combustion collaboration. The parties indefinitely suspended both the joint development and commercial agreements, ending Baker Hughes’ La Porte access and exclusivity, while leaving certain provisions in place. Separately, they amended the license to grant worldwide, perpetual industrial-scale rights with royalties tied to commercial plant operation and preserved Nuovo Pignone’s utility-scale exclusivity. The changes reflect market conditions and Net Power’s decision to halt near-term investment in the prior utility-scale program.

Agreement 1: Net Power and Baker Hughes Affiliates Suspend Joint Development Agreement Indefinitely

  • Agreement type: Suspension Agreement for Amended and Restated Joint Development Agreement
  • Counterparty: Nuovo Pignone and Nuovo Pignone International
  • Signed / Effective: Sep 08 2026 / Jan 01 2026
  • Duration / Termination: Indefinite, by mutual agreement
  • Reason: Pause uneconomic utility-scale turboexpander program

Agreement 2: Net Power and Nuovo Pignone International Suspend Commercial Agreement

  • Agreement type: Suspension Agreement for Commercial Agreement
  • Counterparty: Nuovo Pignone International
  • Signed / Effective: Sep 08 2026 / Sep 08 2026
  • Duration / Termination: Indefinite, by mutual agreement
  • Reason: Halt utility-scale NET Power Platform commercialization

Agreement 3: Net Power Amends License With Nuovo Pignone, Refocusing on Industrial-Scale Plants

  • Agreement type: First Amendment to License Agreement (industrial-scale licensing and royalty framework)
  • Counterparty: Nuovo Pignone and Nuovo Pignone International
  • Signed / Effective: Sep 08 2026 / Jan 01 2026
  • Duration / Termination: Perpetual
  • Reason: Refocus on industrial-scale licensing while preserving utility-scale rights

Original SEC Filing: Net Power Inc. [ NPWR ] - 8-K - Sep. 11, 2026
